question: Should `openclaw/plugin-sdk/archive`, `openclaw/plugin-sdk/root-walk`, and `openclaw/plugin-sdk/secret-file` become stable public plugin contracts, or should this refactor keep those fs-safe operations internal until a narrower plugin API is approved?
rationale: This choice fixes the long-term external plugin compatibility boundary; implementation evidence cannot determine which filesystem capabilities OpenClaw intends to support permanently.

options.title: Approve the three SDK subpaths
options.body: Treat the documented exports as stable external plugin APIs and land them with the existing surface baselines and compatibility expectations.

options.title: Keep the capabilities internal
options.body: Move bundled callers behind existing internal/core facades and remove the new public exports until a focused plugin API proposal is approved.

recommendation.title: Keep the capabilities internal
recommendation.body: Move bundled callers behind existing internal/core facades and remove the new public exports until a focused plugin API proposal is approved.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete owns the current refactor series and has described the proposed public seams and their intended users.
